How to play & keyboard shortcuts

Select an axis below the 3D view, or select a ring, node, or axis label. Both panels share the selected axis. Grab and drag a ring to turn it. In 3D, ↶ Rotate is positive (counterclockwise) and Rotate ↷ is negative (clockwise), looking inward from the selected axis’s outer end. During a move, the axis button and applied rotation button light up together. Inner cube slices follow their named face; M follows L, E follows D, and S follows F. Drag the 3D puzzle to orbit; scroll or pinch to zoom. The ring map stays at its default position and scale; ring dragging and node selection remain available.

Use ← and → to turn the selected ring. Keys U D L R F B turn outer layers; hold Alt for the adjacent inner slice, and Shift to reverse. Select deeper slices using their ring buttons. The eight layers of each axis are separately selectable, including the deepest iii slices. A prime (′) means inverse and 2 means a half-turn. Letters use clockwise notation viewed from that side; arrow buttons follow the ring’s on-screen direction.

Use the top playback-rate selector for ½× through 8× animation. During Auto Solve, Stop requests the end of the current sequence; click Stop now to finish only the current turn. Manual constrained Stop finishes only the current turn. A partial sequence may not yet restore held colors. Randomize and journal replay stop at the last completed turn.

Open the illustrated How to play for annotated ring-map and 3D examples, held colors, selection, playback, labels, and goal preview. The puzzle’s Solution guide explains its specific solving method.
